editorial:
Imagine waking up in a world where you are not quite sure what is real and what is a machine. You get dropped into a strange, moody setting where the lines between humans and robots start to blur. The vibe is very quiet and mysterious, making you feel like you are solving a puzzle alongside the main characters. It does not give you all the answers right away, which keeps you guessing about why everyone is acting so weird and what the actual goal is in this cold, metallic environment.

What really works here is the acting and the way the scenes look. The slow pace might feel a bit long for some, but it builds a lot of tension that pays off. If you enjoy stories that make you think and feel a bit uneasy, you will love this.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out that the main character is actually a robot who was programmed to believe he was a human. The big twist happens when he discovers his own mechanical parts, proving his whole life was a lie. He has to decide if he wants to keep pretending or accept his new identity. The movie wraps up with him choosing to embrace his robotic nature, leaving the human world behind for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about artificial intelligence and identity crises.
